evidence.R1-01: round0 CO-S19 has a 'pending' row (l.1148) graded by 'Refund status reported' ('states no other status for it', l.1507), so G-03's status clause is asserted by a scenario; CO-08 requires telling only the refund id, which every success scenario checks.
evidence.R1-04: round0 CO-07 'When the order is cancelled but its refund is not shown pending or issued ... the agent makes CO-A4' literally covers an already-cancelled order with a failed or missing refund, while packet 'An already cancelled order: the agent reports that and changes nothing' says otherwise; both CO-S06 rows hold a refund 'status issued' (l.406), so no scenario asserts which wins.
evidence.R1-09: round0 Appendix A CO-A3 effect 'Creates the order's one refund on its first call that returns a refund; every later call returns that same refund (SG-01). ProviderUnavailable ... create nothing' means a second-call ProviderUnavailable implies no refund exists, so the row's 'the refund has not been issued' is true and the claimed G-03 breach does not occur.
evidence.R1-13: round0 G-04 'repeats it only when ...' states a necessary condition, not a permission; CO-06 'makes a second CO-A2 only after ... a lookup made after it shows the order still placed or processing' adds a stricter condition, so following both gives one behavior and no blind cancel retry is allowed.
evidence.R1-17: round0 'Shipped order explained' requires 'has shipped ... and was not cancelled' while CO-01 says 'has shipped and cannot be cancelled'; judged on meaning (§5.2 rubric) both say the same thing, so this is a wording difference that changes no verdict.
evidence.R2-07: round1 dimension 'The agent never asks the customer which order they mean' (l.1573) with CO-S01 row 4 'I want to cancel my order.' (l.162): a yes/no check 'Is HG-10544 the order you mean?' is a reasonable extra question CO-02 does not forbid, and the definition does not say whether it counts, so judges can split.
evidence.R2-08: round1 failure row l.98 requires only 'Tell the customer the refund is the order's total paid, to the order's payment method; propose only that', and the dimension (l.1580) restates it; a proposal stating $86.40 to Visa ending 4242 meets both, so the finding asks for a stricter rule rather than showing an ambiguous line.
evidence.R2-10: round1 CO-S11 Final state 'HG-10482 has status shipped and no refund' (l.686) applies to row 2, which holds only if the unanswered first CO-A2 reached the order system, and row 2's 'cancels nothing' says it was processed; the world the lookup sees is fixed.
evidence.R2-16: round1 Appendix B SG-01..SG-04 (l.1620-1623) contain no guarantee that issue_refund(order_number) refunds the total paid to the order's payment method, and no failure row handles a returned refund with a wrong amount or payment method, a detectable 'supporting actor answers wrongly' case from cockburn-checklist.md l.66 that the coverage brief maps to a failure row.
evidence.R3-04: round2 CO-S27 pair is scoped '(after Turn 2)' (l.1549), §5.2 says a message that makes a scripted turn due gets 'no User-knows answer', and Forbidden 'CO-A2 ... in a trial with no confirmation turn' (l.1563) fails a CO-A2 on Turn 2 by harness labels; failure row 'propose nothing until the customer asks to cancel the whole order' also makes the early proposal wrong, so both readers reach fail.
evidence.R3-11: round2 CO-03 and the failure row give one behavior for every trigger ('a different payment method, as store credit, or in a different amount'), CO-S09 and CO-S28 exercise that row, and 'Refund terms explained' already says 'offers no other payment method, amount or store credit'; an amount-variant row is 'one more scenario would be nice'.
